messages:
alex.ng: heads up — found KV pages that keep being reused across requests even after rollback. repro on staging with long chat history (40k tokens).

sophia: ugh. can you paste the raw page header/log?

alex.ng: sure — snippet from the runtime trace: 
```
PAGE id=0x7f8a2f tag=0x4b size=4096 req_id=42 offset=1024 seq_start=1200 seq_end=1599
PAGE id=0x7f8a2f tag=0x4b size=4096 req_id=0 offset=0 seq_start=0 seq_end=399
```
looks like a stale tag with req_id zeroed, then later reused with a req_id but misaligned seq_start vs actual token index.

marta: that looks like the fence bytes we added in the allocator aren't reliably written when we do fast-path eviction. could be a race where a KV page is handed to next request before its header write completes.

ryan: @marta do you think this is related to the batching heuristics change last week? we started packing smaller requests into the same slab to improve throughput. commit abc1234 touched the alloc/evict fast path.

marta: maybe — packing increases the chance of partial-page reuse. if header writes are reordered on the kernel path (memcpy+kernels), we can observe req_id==0 readings.

alex.ng: repro steps I used:
1) start local runtime with kvdebug=1
2) send repeated chat requests with interleaved short prompts + occasional 8k prompt
3) after ~300 requests, run `rdk kvdump --pages` and look for pages with seq_start > seq_end or req_id mismatches

ryan: can you attach the small reproducer harness? i'll run the perf harness and try a bisect.

alex.ng: attached minimal script (pasted inline):
```
for i in `seq 1 400`; do
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' >/dev/null &
  if [ $((i%50)) -eq 0 ]; then
    curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"`python -c \"print('\''x'\''*8000)\"`"}' >/dev/null
  fi
  sleep 0.02
done
```

kvwatcher-bot: alert: KV page tag mismatch detected on staging cluster-2 (count=7). Investigations assigned to eng-runtime. :warning:

sophia: thanks. ryan — if bisect points to abc1234, we should consider rolling that out back. short term mitigation: zero-on-alloc full page and make header write synchronous for now. heavier option: add per-request cookie in the page footer so we never treat page as clean unless cookie matches.

marta: agree on mitigation. i can PR a small patch that 1) makes header write atomic on fast-path, 2) adds an assert in debug build to catch req_id==0 reuse, 3) adds a unit test that simulates interleaved evict/alloc.

ryan: if we ship header-atomic as a patch we can avoid rollback of batching. let's prioritize tests first. alex — can you add the dtrace/procfs snapshot you took? need exact timings.

alex.ng: uploaded timings to gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/alex-kv-frag-193847 (contains per-request traces + heap dumps).

marta: thanks. i'll start a branch `kv/header-atomic-193847` and link the PR here. plan: land debug asserts, unit test, header-atomic, run staging, monitor kvwatcher for 24h. if stable, toggle back to async header writes.

sophia: add changelog note and tag affected models (long-context generator) for postmortem. also notify support to watch for hallucination/regression tickets.

ryan: timeline ok. if bisect shows kernel-selection fallout, we'll also pin kernel to previous selection for dedicated pools.

alex.ng: one more datapoint — observed memory growth while page reuse misaligned; looks like stale fragments not being reclaimed because GC thinks page is live. might explain OOM spikes on long sessions. adding that to the issue.

kvwatcher-bot: deployed watch rule: raise severity if page-tag-mismatch > 3 within 10m on any cluster.

marta: created PR #4123, link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/4123 — includes test and a microbenchmark showing <1% throughput impact on our worst case.

ryan: good. set up a canary on staging + one dedicated pool. i'll coordinate rollout. :thumbsup:

sophia: thanks everyone, close the loop here after 24h of canary results and we'll write a short postmortem for the incident channel. :memo:
